records.context: The 4-tuple ``(index, average_time, cells, figs)`` that :func:`_measure_crop_core` returns, taken straight off the ``AsyncResult`` -- one result, not the list that :func:`process_measure_crop_results` takes, which is why it is re-wrapped as ``[result]`` below. ``index`` is the position in ``files`` and is translated back through ``index_to_file`` so the ledger entry names the field rather than a number. ``cells`` decides the verdict: the success path leaves the ``np.unique(cell_mask)`` array there, while a plain int ``0`` is the cross-process failure sentinel a worker leaves when it caught its own exception, so only that int records a failure. ``figs`` may be an empty key-value mapping -- nothing is drawn unless ``settings['plot']``. records.source: The 4-tuple ``(index, average_time, cells, figs)`` that :func:`_measure_crop_core` returns, taken straight off the ``AsyncResult`` -- one result, not the list that :func:`process_measure_crop_results` takes, which is why it is re-wrapped as ``[result]`` below. ``index`` is the position in ``files`` and is translated back through ``index_to_file`` so the ledger entry names the field rather than a number. ``cells`` decides the verdict: the success path leaves the ``np.unique(cell_mask)`` array there, while a plain int ``0`` is the cross-process failure sentinel a worker leaves when it caught its own exception, so only that int records a failure. ``figs`` may be an empty dict -- nothing is drawn unless ``settings['plot']``. Passing the same field twice is safe for the counters (``completed_jobs`` and ``reported_files`` are sets) but would save its figures twice, so the retry loop calls this only for the attempt that actually returned.
records.translation: Le 4-uplet ``(index, average_time, cells, figs)`` que renvoie :func:`_measure_crop_core`, pris directement sur l'``AsyncResult`` -- un seul résultat, pas la liste attendue par :func:`process_measure_crop_results`, c'est pourquoi il est réenveloppé en ``[result]`` plus bas. ``index`` est la position dans ``files`` et est retraduit via ``index_to_file`` afin que l'entrée du registre nomme le champ plutôt qu'un nombre. ``cells`` décide du verdict : le chemin de réussite y laisse le tableau ``np.unique(cell_mask)``, tandis qu'un simple int ``0`` est la sentinelle d'échec inter-processus qu'un worker laisse lorsqu'il a intercepté sa propre exception, donc seul cet int enregistre un échec. ``figs`` peut être un dict vide -- rien n'est dessiné sans ``settings['plot']``. Passer deux fois le même champ est sans danger pour les compteurs (``completed_jobs`` et ``reported_files`` sont des ensembles) mais enregistrerait ses figures deux fois, donc la boucle de reprise n'appelle ceci que pour la tentative qui a réellement renvoyé un résultat.

records.source: ``apply_async`` hands the error callback only the exception, so the file has to be closed over. Without this hook a worker that died outright vanished entirely: the exception sat on an AsyncResult nobody read, and the run still printed "Successfully completed run".
records.translation: ``apply_async`` ne transmet au callback d'erreur que l'exception, donc le fichier doit être capturé par fermeture.
